newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close lower in thin trade.

text.p: Tel Aviv shares closed lower on Monday in dull trading as investors continued to remain sidelined, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.41 percent, or 0.79 points, to 193.08 on a low all-share turnover of 40 million shekels against 43 million on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index lost 0.38 percent to 202.37.

"Trading was very dull today and the market is stuck. Total volume is simply ridiculous and the most active players are funds who want to improve their results before the end of the year," said Danni Scharia at Capital Securities.
"Several small cap stocks rose sharply on volume of less than 1,500 shekels. This market is dead," Scharia added.
Tadiran, the most active share, lost 0.5 percent to 1,447 on volume of 3.0 million shekels. Tadiran reported a rise in third-quarter earnings per share to $0.59 from $0.54 a year earlier.
Tadiran's parent company Koor Industries fell 0.5 percent to 28,596.
Mofet Israel Technology Fund surged 4.0 percent to 126 after it reported third-quarter net profit of 10.7 million shekels against a loss of 531,000 shekels a year earlier.
"There is a general lack of interest in the market. Today's turnover was one of the lowest we have seen in the last 10 years and there is simply no activity," said Uri Schur at Eyal Securities.

Other active shares include Bank Hapoalim, which gained 0.5 percent to 451 on volume of 2.6 million shekels and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which closed unchanged at 148,049 on turnover of 1.6 million shekels.
